prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows the camera wearer's left and right forearms and hands held up in the immediate foreground (brightest, about 0.2 to 0.5 metres away and 0.1 to 0.3 metres apart), manipulating pliers and a white rod within direct arm's reach while looking down toward a tiled floor and a wooden tray roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres below and in front. No other people are present, though a cat appears on the lower right in frames 1 to 3 and stands upright on its hind legs in front of a glass door in frame 5 (about 1.2 to 1.8 metres away, roughly 0.8 metres beyond the wearer's right hand, facing away toward the window and not looking at the wearer). Across frames 1 to 4, the wearer's hands and arms move closer to the camera and partially occlude the tray and floor tools below, before the viewpoint pitches upward and turns right in frame 5 as the left hand drops mostly out of the lower-left frame and the right arm extends lower in front. The depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground arms and the upright silhouette of the cat and scratching post in frame 5 from the recessed floor plane even during severe motion blur in frame 4, where details are hard to resolve in RGB alone. However, the depth map is unreliable on the bright glass window in frame 5 and dark furniture edges on the right, rendering the window pane as an uniformly black far void and merging the blurred space between the arms into a dark blob in frame 4.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the camera wearer's two foreground arms (about 0.2 to 0.5 metres from the lens) as separate masks in frames 1 to 3 that merge into a single large 'person' mask in frame 4 as the hands approach the camera, while no other people are present in the room. It detects the cat entering at the bottom right in frame 2 (about 1.5 metres away, below and behind the right arm) and reveals its silhouette standing upright in front of the window in frame 5 (facing the glass away from the wearer, about 0.8 metres in front of the wearer's lowered right arm) as an unlabelled cutout occluding the light-blue 'tv' mask. While the pliers and white tube held within the wearer's grasp (0.3 metres away) and the screwdrivers, tray, and scratching post on the floor (1.0 to 1.5 metres away) remain completely unsegmented, the map helps track the boundary of the wearer's limbs against the cluttered background across the camera's upward tilt in frame 5. Compared to RGB alone, the map makes the partial entry of the cat in frame 2 immediately salient via a distinct pink mask at the lower-right edge. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable in class labels and object boundaries: it splits the wearer's own left and right arms into separate 'person' instances, misclassifies the left arm as a 'cell phone' and background floor items as 'person' in frame 2, hallucinates a giant 'person' blob across the blurred background in frame 4, and mislabels the bright window in frame 5 as a 'tv'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map tracks the fine 3D articulation of the camera wearer's left hand in frames 1 to 3 (on the left, about 0.3 to 0.4 metres from the viewpoint) and right hand in frame 5 (lower right, about 0.4 metres away), with no other people present in the scene. In frames 1 to 3, the magenta hand skeletons show the left fingers curled around the white rod and pliers within immediate reach while gradually opening and shifting upward, before disappearing completely during the close-up blur of frame 4 and the camera's turn toward the window in frame 5, where only the lowered right hand is tracked. The map provides explicit joint locations and finger curvature for the active hand in frames 1 to 3 and frame 5 that are partially self-occluded or blended into skin tones in the RGB frames. However, the pose estimation is unreliable for the rest of the body and the second hand: it completely misses the wearer's right hand in frames 1 to 4 and left hand in frame 5, and in frame 2 it hallucinates a yellow full-body skeleton along the upright right forearm and pliers handle as if a miniature person were standing at 0.3 metres distance.
